newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks drop 1.35 percent on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks drop 1.35 percent on profit-taking.

text.p: Toronto's stock market sold off almost 1.4 percent on Monday as anxious investors reaped profits ahead of closely watched comments by U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan starting on Tuesday.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index tumbled 90.80 points to finish at 6647.39 in light trading.
Jim Mountain, ScotiaMcLeod's managing director of private client equity trading, said that market players were awaiting Greenspan's congressional testimony.
Greenspan sparked a selloff in equity markets worldwide after warning against irrational exuberance in December.
"We get nervous profit-taking in the face of uncertainty," Mountain said. "Undoubtedly he (Greenspan) is going to have more comments on equities."
Greenspan is scheduled to deliver his two-day, semi-annual Humphrey-Hawkins testimony to a House of Representatives subcommittee at 1400 EDT/1800 GMT on Tuesday.
Canadian investors also shed issues in a belated reaction to New York's 130-point decline on Friday.
"Part of what you saw in Toronto today was a knee-jerk reaction to the big drop-off Friday in the United States," Mountain added.
Another trader said Toronto was due for a broad-based retreat after the market hit new highs last week.
All of Toronto's 14 sectors retreated, led by a 2.75 percent drop in golds. Utilities, conglomerates, financial services and retailing all shed more than one percent.
About 67.5 million shares were traded worth C$1.2 billion ($871 million.)
Declining issues nearly doubled gainers 633 to 319 while another 321 ended flat.
BCE Inc., Canada's largest publicly traded firm, fell 1.15 to 41.10 on almost 1.4 million shares. Analysts said the telecommunications conglomerate was hit by profit-taking.

Oxford Properties Group Inc. dipped 1.60 to 32. Prudential Insurance Co. of America said its Canadian arm will sell its Canadian real estate portfolio to a joint venture of Oxford and GE Capital Canada Inc. for C$455.8 million ($331 million).
